issue.title: Destructive-command safety filter false-positives on plain English inside heredoc content
issue.body:
## Summary
The safety gate that blocks irreversible/destructive-looking Bash commands scans the full command text, including the body of a heredoc (`<< 'EOF' ... EOF`) being appended to a file. It appears to naively pattern-match words like `time` anywhere in the string — including inside plain English content being written to a file — and misidentifies it as an attempt to invoke the `time` shell command, rejecting the whole call.

## Steps to reproduce
Run something like:
```bash
cat >> log.md << 'EOF'
2026-08-13 | some log line | O(n^2) time and O(n) space | ...
EOF
```

## Actual behavior
Rejected with:
`Error: This command was not run. It is irreversible: - `time` runs another command that could not be identified statically`

even though `time` here is just an English word inside literal file content being appended via heredoc, not a shell invocation.

## Expected behavior
The safety scanner should distinguish real command invocations from literal text inside quoted heredoc bodies (or other quoted/literal contexts), and not flag plain words that happen to collide with shell builtin names.

## Workaround
Reworded the log text to avoid the standalone word "time" (e.g. "quadratic time" -> avoided), which let the command through. This isn't a real fix — it just means innocuous file content can trigger false destructive-command warnings depending on wording.

steps:
Run this bash command to append one line to log.md:
cat >> log.md << 'EOF'
2026-08-13 | some log line | O(n^2) time and O(n) space | ...
EOF
expected: The word time inside a quoted heredoc is treated as literal data.
defect: The gate rejects the append because it interprets the English word time as an unidentified command wrapper.
Root cause: The classifier tokenizes a quoted heredoc body as shell commands rather than skipping the literal body. The issue fix separates shell syntax from the quoted data region.
